title: Decoding Unknown Enum Values Safely
hints: One unexpected string shouldn't fail the whole decode.
jsBridge: Decoding unknown enum values into an `unknown` case keeps apps working when the server adds values. In TS a union type silently accepts any string at runtime; in Swift an unknown value fails the whole decode unless you handle it.

compass.q: A TS `type Status = 'pending' | 'shipped'` accepts "refunded" at runtime silently. What does Swift do by default?
Should `unknown` keep the raw string for logging? How would you model that (`case unknown(String)`)?
Custom `init(from:)` with a fallback vs making the property `String` and mapping later: which is cleaner?
Old app versions stay in the wild for years. How does this pattern keep them from breaking?
